rgb: The scene takes place in an indoor room with an exposed ceiling grid above, a light-colored couch with cushions about 3 to 5 metres in front of and out of reach of the camera wearer, a lamp partly visible on the left edge at about 3 to 5 metres, and a back wall with a dark door roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres away on the left and within reach. depth: The monocular depth map orders the indoor scene into clear depth layers: in the background (roughly 3 to 5 metres away, out of the camera wearer's and opponent's arm's reach), a vertical perforated Connect Four game board sits at the bottom center and rises into view from frame 1 to frame 4, while the camera wearer's own right arm and hand holding a red token enter from the bottom right in frame 5 as the brightest, farthest surface (~3 to 5 metres away). Directly behind the board (roughly 3 to 5 metres from the camera wearer and 3 to 5 metres behind the board), a woman wearing dark glasses and a puffy jacket sits on a couch facing away and looking downward toward the board between them, with the couch cushions extending behind her to the right and left at roughly 3 to 5 metres and a floor lamp at the far left edge at ~2.0 metres. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint pitches downward and moves slightly farther from the table from frames 1 to 4 before tilting slightly back in frame 5, while the seated woman leans backward in frame 3 to extend her left hand over the top of the board (~3 to 5 metres from the camera) to drop a yellow token, then lowers her arm to her left side in frame 4 and leans forward from the couch in frame 5 as the camera wearer's right arm reaches up and partially occludes her left side. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the metric separation between the background board, the woman's reaching hand, the couch cushions, and the nearby walls (which rise into visible values within roughly 0.5 to 1.5 metres) immediately apparent, and it even resolves the depth through several circular holes of the game grid. However, the depth map is unreliable inside some of the small circular cutouts of the Connect Four board—where foreground depth bleeds inconsistently with the background plastic—and along the nearby ceiling grid and recessed hallway, which are compressed into a nearly uniform black region.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the primary background actors and furniture against an unlabelled foreground: the seated woman in front of the camera wearer (~3 to 5 metres away, facing away from the camera and looking down at the game) is segmented as a 'person' across all five frames, flanked right and left by the sofa cushions behind her (~3 to 5 metres away) labelled as 'couch' from frame 2 onward, while the Connect Four board at the bottom center (~3 to 5 metres away, out of arm's reach of both people) is segmented in frames 3 to 5. In frame 5, the camera wearer's reaching right forearm and hand (~3 to 5 metres away on the lower right) are segmented as a second 'person' instance that overlaps and partially occludes the couch on the right and the seated woman's left arm behind the board. Across the 5-frame sequence, the segmented 'person' mask of the woman shifts higher in the frame and expands to the right in frames 3 and 4 as she leans backward and extends her left arm over and then beside the board, while the board mask at the bottom grows larger from frame 3 to 4 as the camera tilts down. While segmentation sharply delineates the outer silhouette of the reaching arms, torso, and furniture boundaries that blend into the busy office foreground in RGB, it suffers from severe semantic and boundary errors. Specifically, it misclassifies the vertical open-front zipper and collar gap of the woman's jacket as a 'tie' in every frame, mislabels the blue Connect Four grid as a 'laptop' in frames 3 to 5 (missing it entirely in frames 1 and 2), splits the sofa cushions into multiple 'couch' and 'bed' instances, and completely omits the yellow and red game tokens, ceiling, walls, and floor lamp.
pose: The skeleton map tracks the 2D keypoints of the woman seated roughly 3 to 5 metres in front of and out of reach of the camera wearer: across all five frames, a cluster of yellow facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) shows her head centered and facing away from the camera wearer while angled slightly downward toward the game area below. In frames 1 and 2, only her head keypoints and a nearly horizontal yellow line connecting her right and left shoulders are detected, as her lower torso and arms are occluded or cropped at the bottom of the frame behind the game board. In frame 3, as she leans backward out of arm's reach of the board (~3 to 5 metres from the camera), her full upper-body trapezoid (shoulders and hips), right arm, and raised left arm appear in yellow alongside a dense cluster of magenta left-hand keypoints positioned just above the right side of the board where she holds the yellow token. In frame 4, the skeleton captures her left arm extending downward and to the image-right as her magenta left hand drops to waist level beside the couch cushion, while in frame 5 her torso shifts forward and a magenta hand skeleton reappears near her left shoulder. This map makes her head orientation, shoulder tilt, and left-arm trajectory explicit without visual clutter, but it is highly unreliable in frame 5, where it fails to assign a separate body skeleton to the camera wearer and instead fuses the camera wearer's background right hand (~3 to 5 metres away) onto the nearby woman's left arm and hand keypoints (~1.0 metre away), while also missing her torso in frames 1 and 2 and her right hand throughout.
